name: ProSpend
description: Spend management for a mid-market finance team: expenses, bills, purchase orders, budgets, virtual cards, and payments. Bootstrapped in Australia by Sharon Nouh. Sold in 2025 to ISH, a UK software group, so she could expand in the UK with a local partner and still run the product.

mentions.evidence: Company-stated, Practical Founders, May 2026. No revenue total in the source. About 1,000 customers and 50 employees. Annual contracts roughly $15,000 to $40,000. Bootstrapped for about 10 years, then a strategic sale, not a distress exit.
mentions.indieAngle: Expenses, bills, and cards in one product, sold through the accountants who already have the client.

whyItPrints: A mid-size finance team hates the expense pile and does not want an enterprise suite. The contract size in the article is the mid-market, not a seat at a few dollars.
whyThisMatters:
ProSpend is expenses, bills, purchase orders, budgets, and cards for a mid-market finance team. Sharon Nouh built it in Australia, bootstrapped, for about ten years. In 2025 she sold it to a UK software group so the product could expand there with a local partner, and she kept running it.

The article does not give a revenue total. I am not writing one. About a thousand customers. About fifty people. A yearly contract in a range that starts in the mid five figures. She describes it as a strategic sale, not a rescue. May 2026. Self-reported.

You pay so the expense pile and the cards are one system, at a price a mid-size company can sign.

ISH is the UK buyer, in 2025. She stayed on the product so the UK expansion had a local partner. Ten years bootstrapped is the runway before that sale. The contract range is the only money figure the article gives. A thousand customers and fifty people are the size lines.
